# Chestnut of Cost Report (`chestnut-of-cost-report`)

Cost report and audit support for nursing homes: patient days by payer tied out between the census, the cost report draft and the Medicare PS&R, and the prepared-by-client list for auditors, the bank and the Medicare contractor with overdue and due-soon items. Resident identifiers are masked before results reach the model.

**Chestnut never files a cost report or sends anything to a Medicare contractor.**

Evergreen ver 1 · Financial services · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`evergreen-core`](../evergreen-core)

```bash
npx -y chestnut-of-cost-report demo
npx -y chestnut-of-cost-report mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

A fictional Cedar Hollow 2025 fiscal year, checked on 15 April 2026. The census has 1274 patient days: Medicare A 99, Medicaid 974 and other 201. Planted:

- The cost report draft has 971 Medicaid days and 1271 in total. It left out R1806's three hospital leave days in May.
- The PS&R has 95 Medicare A covered days against 99 on the census, so four days look unbilled or denied.
- The bad debt listing for the Medicare contractor was due 10 April, and the year-end AR aging is due 20 April.

[`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `chestnut_check` | Tie patient days by payer between the census, the cost report draft and the PS&R, and list PBC items due. | runs |
| `chestnut_write_report` | Write chestnut-tie-out.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and chestnut-tie-out.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/chestnut). | runs |
| `chestnut_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `chestnut_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `chestnut_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `chestnut_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `cost_report_file` | Chestnut never files a cost report or sends anything to a Medicare contractor. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `chestnut_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `census` (required) | Census for the fiscal year under --root |
| `cost_report` (required) | Cost report draft days under --root: payer type (medicare_a, medicaid, other, total) and days |
| `psr` | Optional PS&R summary under --root: Medicare Part A covered days |
| `pbc` | Optional prepared-by-client list under --root: item, requested by, owner, due, received |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: tolerance_days, count_leave_days |
| `start` (required) | First day of the fiscal year (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `end` (required) | Last day of the fiscal year (YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `as_of` | Date for PBC deadlines (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx chestnut-of-cost-report inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Census (`census`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `resident_id` | text (masked) | Resident ID, Resident #, Resident Number, Res ID, Res #, MRN, Medical Record Number, Client ID |
| `resident_name` | text (masked) | Resident, Resident Name, Name, Patient, Patient Name, Client Name, Resident Full Name |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Facility Name, Building, Location, Fac, Center |
| `from` (required) | date | From, Start, Start Date, Effective Date, Begin Date, From Date, Admit Date, Census Date |
| `to` | date | To, End, End Date, Thru, Through, Thru Date, Through Date, To Date |
| `payer` (required) | text | Payer, Payer Name, Primary Payer, Pay Source, Payer Source, Payor, Payor Name, Insurance |
| `payer_type` | text | Payer Type, Payor Type, Payer Class, Payer Category, Pay Type |
| `level` | text | Level, Level of Care, Care Level, Rate Type, Rate Level, Room Type, Accommodation, RUG |
| `bed_status` | text | Bed Status, Status, Census Status, Action, Census Action, Leave Type |
| `room` | text | Room, Room Bed, Bed, Room/Bed, Unit |

### Cost report days (`cost_report`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `payer_type` (required) | text | Payer Type, Program, Title, Line, Payer |
| `days` (required) | number | Days, Patient Days, Inpatient Days, Census Days |

### PS&R (`psr`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `days` (required) | number | Days, Covered Days, Utilization Days, Paid Days |

### PBC list (`pbc`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `item` (required) | text | Item, Request, Description, PBC Item |
| `requested_by` | text | Requested By, Requester, For |
| `owner` | text | Owner, Assigned To, Preparer |
| `due` | date | Due, Due Date |
| `received_on` | date | Received, Sent, Provided On, Done |

## Settings file (`chestnut_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `tolerance_days` | Allowed difference in days (default 0) |
| `count_leave_days` | Count leave and hospital hold days as patient days (default true; follow your state and cost report instructions) |

## Memory

`chestnut_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `chestnut_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `tie_out_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `evergreen-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "chestnut-of-cost-report": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "chestnut-of-cost-report",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add chestnut-of-cost-report -- npx -y chestnut-of-cost-report mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
chestnut-of-cost-report tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
chestnut-of-cost-report sources               # the columns each input is read from
chestnut-of-cost-report inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
chestnut-of-cost-report call chestnut_check '{"census":"<census>","cost_report":"<cost_report>","start":"<start>","end":"<end>"}'
chestnut-of-cost-report eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
chestnut-of-cost-report demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
